what: DT Midstream owns natural gas pipelines and storage, mostly serving the Appalachian shale fields and the Gulf Coast, and charges fees for moving and holding gas rather than owning it.
customers: Gas producers in Appalachia and Louisiana, utilities and power generators, on long-term contracts.
money: interstate and intrastate transport, storage and gathering
collecting gas from wellheads to the pipeline network
moat: Pipelines are close to impossible to permit and build in the United States today, so the ones already in the ground earn fees under contracts that do not depend on the gas price.
risks: Revenue depends on producers keeping the pipelines full, which depends on gas prices they control
25 times earnings for an infrastructure business growing in the mid single digits
opportunities: A 35.5% net margin and $533M of free cash flow on $1.3B of revenue: the economics of toll roads
Analysts see about 29% upside, with 15 covering the stock
Data centre electricity demand is lifting gas-fired power generation, which needs pipeline capacity
watch: Contracted volumes and progress on new pipeline projects.
